_comment: The round-trip test fixture for this video. split-cameras.py conforms `source` onto a strict CFR grid as `program`, then rebuilds one synthetic camera raw per angle in `shots`. Nothing here describes the finished edit -- that is read back off the programme by shot-detect.py.
_why: First non-a16z fixture, and the film that forced person-identity angle detection: an hour-long Ukrainska Pravda studio roundtable, 25 fps, 1080p, four people against one black backdrop. Also the first film through the 25 fps audio-boundary path and the hour-long clustering path.

stagger._comment: Seeded so the same manifest rebuilds the same tapes. Ranges are seconds; the draw is converted to whole frames before anything uses it.

conform._comment: One generation, high quality: everything downstream is scored against this file, so its own loss is the noise floor of the whole test.

render._comment: The tapes. cq 16 keeps generational loss well below the structural differences the comparator is looking for.

verify._comment: freeze_db -60 is far below anything real footage registers, so a freeze found inside a live span means the graph put the wrong picture there. cover_frac is loose on purpose: freezedetect needs a moment to declare a freeze, so the first fraction of a gap never counts.
